briefings.title: 0 to $250M ARR in 12 Months: Genspark & the Global Knowledge Worker | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Wen Sang shares how GenSpark scaled from $0 to $250M ARR in 12 months by building an agentic AI workspace that orchestrates over 70 frontier and open-weight models to automate busy work for a billion-plus knowledge workers.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Wen Sang shares how GenSpark scaled from $0 to $250M ARR in 12 months by building an agentic AI workspace that orchestrates over 70 frontier and open-weight models to automate busy work for a billion-plus knowledge workers.

## Company Growth & Scaling Metrics
* **Explosive Revenue Growth:** 
  * **Zero to $50M ARR:** Reached within 5 months of launching the individual product in April (driven by 2 million users in 45 days via product-led, bottom-up growth on X and YouTube).
  * **$100M ARR:** Reached at 9 months.
  * **$250M ARR:** Reached at 12 months, alongside raising approximately $645M to $700M in funding.
* **Enterprise Expansion:** 
  * **GenSpark for Business:** Launched in November (right before Thanksgiving) after employees brought individual usage into corporate settings and demanded enterprise features like centralized billing, SOC 2 Type 2, and SSO.
  * **Customer Base:** Reached 6,000+ business clients globally within 6 months across industries including system integration, consulting firms, advertising agencies, consumer brands, and manufacturing.

## Founding Team & Origins
* **Pedigree and Background:** 
  * **Wen Sang (Co-Founder & COO):** Automotive engineer by training with a PhD from MIT (2013); previously built and ran a vertical SaaS company for municipalities and commercial real estate for 8–9 years (backed by Coast Ventures and Y Combinator) before selling it in 2022.
  * **Eric:** Early team member at Microsoft Bing working with Satya Nadella; prior to GenSpark, built a voice AI and deep learning company from 0 to $5.5B in value alongside co-founders K and Ray.
  * **Ray:** Spent 14 years at Google building early search ranking technologies.
  * **K:** Spent ~8 years at Google building search ranking technologies.
  * **Lendroy:** Enterprise tech leader who spent ~10 years at Google before building teams at Pinterest, YouTube, and TikTok.
* **The Hard Pivot:** 
  * **Initial Product (Late '23 / Early '24):** Originally built a next-generation personalized AI search engine that grew to 5 million users.
  * **The Pivot:** Realized search had a lot of buzz but little monetization and that Google would replicate basic search; asked why people search (to get work done), and pivoted in early '25 to leverage newly emerged reasoning capabilities to build the first version of the AI workspace.

## Product Architecture & "Mixture of Agents"
* **Multi-Model Orchestration:** 
  * **70+ Models Integrated:** The platform sits on top of and orchestrates over 70 frontier models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) and open-weight model providers (Fireworks, Fell, AWS Bedrock, GCP).
  * **Specialized Routing:** Assigns tasks to the model best suited for them—GPT models for reasoning and planning, Claude models for coding and HTML rendering, Google models for images, video, and artistic work, and open-weight models for fast, cost-effective Python scripting and visualization in Jupyter Notebooks.
* **Full-Stack Automation Features:**
  * **GenSpark Superagent:** Acts like an FSD (Full Self-Driving) system for knowledge work; users command outcomes rather than manually typing, formatting, or building models cell-by-cell or pixel-by-pixel.
  * **Agentbase:** A newly launched capability that lets users command GenSpark to build lightweight custom software applications like CRMs, ATS, and lightweight ERPs tailored to their exact preferences and data workflows, reducing traditional SaaS bloat.

## Enterprise Adoption & Workplace Impact
* **Death by 1,000 Pilots:** Enterprise companies struggling with IT buying 20 to 50 seats of dozens of different tools found success through bottom-up employee budgets ($50–$100/month) that allowed successful AI use cases to bubble up organically.
* **Executive Leadership:** High-profile adoption—such as CEO Miguel at a major global system integrator—proves that when leadership uses AI as a daily power user, it fundamentally changes organizational culture.
* **Real-World Use Cases:** 
  * **Bank Loan Consulting:** Dallas-based bank loan consultant Scott uses GenSpark to perform market analysis, build full financial models (P&L, balance sheets, cash flow scenarios), and generate presentations in hours/days instead of weeks/months, allowing him to cut out outsourced analysts, retain all margins, and serve 5x more clients.

## Notable Quotes
> "In the past, we human beings, we are the production engine. Um, we get onto, you know, all kinds of work, may it be building a financial model, crafting a document, building a presentation. We do it hands-on... Now, with GenSpark, you don't do that anymore."
> — **Wen Sang**

> "The world of everybody kneeling before one AI god is long gone now. We're seeing a lot more open-weight models, the floor is rising, and we're continuously seeing... high performance frontier models coming out."
> — **Wen Sang**

> "What we're building at GenSpark is not the next generation of software, no. We're building the next generation users of the software."
> — **Wen Sang**

briefings.title: AI Has a Memory Problem | Gelsinger, SK hynix & More | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: AI demand is outstripping memory supply, creating a "memory wall" bottleneck where high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is thermally and bitwise inefficient yet remains the necessary stopgap until advanced stacked architectures arrive later this decade.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** AI demand is outstripping memory supply, creating a "memory wall" bottleneck where high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is thermally and bitwise inefficient yet remains the necessary stopgap until advanced stacked architectures arrive later this decade.

## The AI Memory Bottleneck: Why Memory is the Limit
* **Insatiable Token Demand:** **Pat Gelsinger** noted a threefold problem: insatiable demand for AI, rapidly growing context windows and model sizes, and the necessity for extremely low first-token latency.
* **The von Neumann Architectural Tax:** **Vijay Shilpiekandula** explained that modern AI inherits an 80-year-old von Neumann architecture where processors sit far from memory, creating a narrow highway (data bottleneck) between the computational "factory" and the memory "warehouse."
* **Systemic Memory Shift:** **Hoshik Kim** stated that memory is no longer viewed merely as a commodity cost, but as a core investment and foundational infrastructure for AI data centers.

## HBM's Limitations and the "Waffle Maker" Production Problem
* **HBM Imperfections:** **Pat Gelsinger** called HBM a "lousy memory" that is thermally constrained (creating a thermal sandwich), shoreline bandwidth-limited, and bitwise inefficient (sacrificing four bits of traditional DRAM for every HBM bit created).
* **The "Waffle Squeeze":** **Andrew Homan** used a waffle maker analogy to illustrate that manufacturing HBM is significantly more complex and slower than commodity DRAM, severely limiting output.
* **Compound Yield Losses:** **Hoshik Kim** explained that HBM requires significantly larger die spaces (roughly three times bigger, known as "HBM squeeze") and stacks DRAM 12 to 16 levels high, resulting in compounding yield losses across front-end wafers, TSV stacking, and micro-bumping.

## Industry Consolidation and Changing Business Models
* **Survival of the Fittest:** **Louis Delahaye** highlighted that the memory industry has consolidated from roughly 20 players down to three primary leaders: SK hynix, Samsung, and Micron.
* **Custom Designs vs. Commodities:** **Andrew Homan** pointed out that tight co-optimization between logic (GPUs) and memory makes suppliers harder to swap, moving HBM away from a pure commodity. **Pat Gelsinger** added that the shift toward custom stacked memory designs will disrupt traditional JEDEC-governed business models.

## Geopolitical Realities and Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
* **Concentrated Geopolitics:** **Vijay Shilpiekandula** noted that front-end memory is concentrated in Korea, packaging is in Taiwan, and NAND is in Japan. 
* **Lack of Resilience:** **Pat Gelsinger** warned that the tech supply chain lacks resilience, noting that a three-week blockade of the Taiwan Strait would brown out the industry, and observed that building a major semiconductor factory takes about four years and roughly six years to achieve profitability.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Breakthrough Memory Architectures:** **Pat Gelsinger** predicts that novel memory architectures (such as stacked memory directly on or integrated into compute layers by companies like Dmatrix, Next Silicon, and acquisitions like Nvidia's purchase of Grock) will achieve 10x to 50x better bandwidth than shoreline-limited HBM, fundamentally changing the industry by the end of the decade.
* **Persistent Shortages:** **Pat Gelsinger** and **Andrew Homan** assert that supply limits and strong demand for HBM will persist for several more years, with no quick fix for supply constraints regardless of capital investments.
* **Long-Term Contracting:** **Hoshik Kim** notes that memory makers are shifting away from pure commodity models toward contract-based, long-term agreements lasting five years or more.

## Notable Quotes
> "HBM is a lousy memory... You're stacking DRAM. DRAM doesn't like to be stacked because essentially you're creating a thermal sandwich... It is just the best one we have right now." 
> — *Pat Gelsinger*

> "We semis investors sleep like a baby... but we wake up every 3 hours to check what's going on in the Asian markets." 
> — *Vijay Shilpiekandula*

> "Memory is no longer a cost anymore; we see memory as an investment to AI infrastructure." 
> — *Hoshik Kim*

briefings.title: AI and Jobs series: How entry level jobs are changing in an AI era
briefings.tldr: Entry-level jobs are transforming as AI automates routine tasks, with employers increasingly prioritizing applied skills, human judgment, and AI fluency over traditional degrees.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Entry-level jobs are transforming as AI automates routine tasks, with employers increasingly prioritizing applied skills, human judgment, and AI fluency over traditional degrees.

## The Impact of AI on Entry-Level Roles & Work Redesign
* **Productivity and Work Redesign:** According to PwC's Global AI and Jobs Barometer, organizations in AI-exposed sectors that proactively redesign work see a **threefold increase in productivity**.
* **Task Automation vs. Human Skills:** Routine cognitive and repetitive tasks are heavily automated by AI. However, demand for human skills (judgment, problem-solving, critical thinking, relationship building) has experienced a **twofold growth rate** in AI-exposed sectors.
* **The "Seniorization" of Skills:** Employers are asking entry-level workers for **seven times greater "seniorized" skills**—competencies historically developed in the first three to four years of a career—upfront.

## Hiring Shifts and Report Findings
* **Resilient Hiring Trends:** Dire headlines regarding entry-level job destruction are not yet backed up by data; many organizations are intentionally increasing hiring to protect future leadership pipelines. One organization cited in the WEF/PwC report increased entry-level hiring by **25%** to ensure future leadership.
* **Shifting Employer Criteria:** Data from the WEF and PwC report shows that **81% of employers** prioritize applied experience, compared to only **34%** prioritizing degrees. 
* **PwC Evolution:** Peter Brown noted that when he joined PwC, there were **17 to 18 entry-level entry points**, which has now been streamlined to about **five**, shifting focus from specific badges and universities to potential and skills.

## Global Survey Insights
* **PwC Hopes and Fears Survey:** As the largest global survey of workers covering some **55,000 workers**, results show that younger workers are more optimistic than anxious regarding AI, though they still navigate broader pressures like the cost-of-living crisis.
* **The Skills vs. Domain Expertise Balance:** While domain expertise remains necessary, employers increasingly demand "AI fluency"—requiring workers to experiment with AI tools and build agility.

## Practical Advice for New Graduates from Industry Leaders
* **Focus on Outcomes, Not Tasks (Karina Cortez, Cornerstone OnDemand):** New grads must focus on wisdom and strategic outcomes rather than rote tasks; focusing purely on tasks risks obsolescence as efficiency tools automate routine work.
* **Lean Into Fear (Karina Cortez):** Graduates should embrace uncomfortable opportunities and "say yes" to challenges, noting that personal growth stems directly from stepping into the unknown. Cortez herself takes "vibe coding classes" to stay current.
* **Embrace Non-Linear Career Paths (Maria Flynn, Jobs for the Future):** A first job is rarely a dream job or a permanent destination; drawing from her own early experience as an entry-level government worker in Philadelphia with five other women, Flynn advises young workers to treat every role as a learning vehicle to identify skills and preferences.
* **Maintain Passion and Agility (Peter Brown, PwC):** Brown encourages graduates to pursue their passions, reject traditional job titles in favor of skills development, experiment with AI tools, and aggressively build interpersonal leadership and teamwork capabilities.

## Notable Quotes
> "The organizations getting ahead are fundamentally breaking down work and looking at, what is it the outcome they're trying to achieve? What's the role of technology, what's the role of the human being?"  
> — **Peter Brown**

> "If you're a new grad, [and] you are focusing just on the tasks to be done, you are going to get left behind from the people who are actually able to level up, if you will, and really think about the outcome impact."  
> — **Karina Cortez**

> "Where you start is not going to be where you finish... your first job is not going to be the job you have forever. But yet, every job, including that first job, can really give you a wealth of information and experience and skills that you can build upon."  
> — **Maria Flynn**

briefings.title: AT&T CEO on Earnings, Mobile Subscriber Gains, AI
briefings.tldr: AT&T reported a strong second quarter, adding 432,000 monthly wireless phone subscribers and a record 370,000 fiber net adds, driven by multi-year capital investments and a successful convergence strategy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
AT&T reported a strong second quarter, adding 432,000 monthly wireless phone subscribers and a record 370,000 fiber net adds, driven by multi-year capital investments and a successful convergence strategy. CEO John Stankey expressed confidence in sustaining this momentum through 2028 while highlighting the company's critical infrastructure role in the upcoming AI era.

## Financial Results & Q2 Performance
* **Subscriber Growth:** 
  * **Wireless Additions:** Added **432,000** monthly wireless phone subscribers in Q2, beating analyst expectations of **325,000**.
  * **Fiber Net Adds:** Reached a record **370,000** fiber net adds during the quarter.
* **Broadband & Mobile Convergence:** 
  * **Convergence Rate:** **42.5%** of households purchasing broadband also buy mobile phone service from AT&T (rising to **45%** when normalized for the recently acquired Lumen footprint).
  * **Customer Benefits:** Multi-product customers are more lucrative, exhibit lower churn, and show higher brand affinity.
* **Financial Metrics:** 
  * Growth manifested in accelerated service revenue growth and accelerated EBITDA growth.
  * Achieved growth in business strategic services for the first time in a long period.
  * Margin performance reached record levels for the company.

## Market Positioning & Competitive Landscape
* **The Convergence Strategy:** Providing world-class networks in both wireless and fixed broadband covers **98%** of a customer's internet needs on a single bill with unified support infrastructure.
* **Pricing and Market Stratification:** 
  * Rejecting the "price war" characterization, Stankey described the market as stratified.
  * AT&T traditionally played well upmarket with high-performing symmetrical gigabit services and robust wireless plans.
  * Recent focus on value-oriented offerings yielded new account additions at a **three-year high**, improving down-market capture without sacrificing margins.
* **Competitive Moats (Urban vs. Rural):** 
  * Satellite services (like Starlink) and cable companies dominate less densely populated and rural areas.
  * AT&T's historical investments focus on dense urban and suburban metro areas, making it difficult for competitors to replicate hard-to-reach infrastructure (such as stadiums).

## Artificial Intelligence & Network Infrastructure
* **AI ROI and Internal Efficiency:** 
  * Disciplined AI investments in software development, customer service channels, engineering applications, and pricing support algorithms are delivering strong returns.
  * Differentiated between table-stakes efficiencies (which get competed away into lower prices or better service) and strategic advantages (like pricing and network yield software).
* **AI Era Readiness:** 
  * Symmetrical networks (offering as much upstream bandwidth as downstream bandwidth) are viewed as indispensable for future AI workloads, alongside chips, memory, and data centers.

## Capital Allocation & Share Repurchases
* **CapEx Cycle Contrast:** Unlike tech companies currently spending heavily to raise capital and build out AI infrastructure, AT&T has largely completed its multi-year asset investment cycle.
* **Share Buybacks:** The company is accelerating the pace of planned share repurchases.
* **Market Valuation:** Stankey characterized the current market as experiencing a temporary "dislocation" and rotation out of AT&T stock due to capital chasing AI tech opportunities, but believes the market will eventually recognize the value of AT&T's indispensable infrastructure.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Sustained Growth:** AT&T expects its current execution and growth momentum to sustain itself through **2028** — John Stankey.
* **Satellite Partnership Timeline:** AT&T will be able to solve out-of-range connectivity gaps via satellite industry partnerships by **this time next year** — John Stankey.

## Notable Quotes
> "And as a result of that, we expect that that's gonna sustain itself through '28. So we're we're executing well. We're hitting on all the cylinders and the engine."
> — John Stankey

> "I think there's been a stratification of pricing for customers depending on what kind of services they wanna buy. [...] I don't consider that a price war. I consider that meeting market needs."
> — John Stankey

> "I do believe that the market will eventually understand that what we have built is indispensable for the kind of workloads we're going to see in this AI environment working forward..."
> — John Stankey

briefings.title: Alphabet 2026 Q2 Earnings Call
briefings.tldr: Alphabet reported Q2 2026 revenue of $119.8 billion, up 24% year-over-year, driven by strong momentum in Cloud (up 82%) and Search (up 17%).
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Alphabet reported Q2 2026 revenue of $119.8 billion, up 24% year-over-year, driven by strong momentum in Cloud (up 82%) and Search (up 17%). Despite operating income of $40.8 billion, capital expenditures rose to $44.9 billion for the quarter, leading to a negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion as the company accelerates technical infrastructure investments to meet surging AI demand.

## Financial Performance & Capital Allocation
- **Consolidated Financials:** 
  - Revenue reached **$119.8 billion**, up 24% year-over-year (23% in constant currency), marking the 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.
  - Operating income grew **30% to $40.8 billion** with an operating margin of 34%.
  - Net income and earnings per share increased significantly, driven primarily by unrealized gains in the equity securities portfolio ($98 billion in other income/expenses).
  - Operating cash flow was **$39.1 billion** for Q2 and **$185.7 billion** for the trailing 12 months.
  - Cash and marketable securities ended at **$242.5 billion**, including $87.1 billion of marketable equity securities; long-term debt stood at **$98.2 billion**.
- **Capital Expenditures & Cash Flow:**
  - Q2 CapEx was **$44.9 billion**, with ~60% spent on servers and 40% on data centers and networking equipment.
  - Free cash flow was **negative $5.9 billion** in Q2 due to high CapEx investments.
  - The Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of **$0.22 per share**, payable in September.
- **Capital Structure Philosophy:** 
  - Operating cash flow is the primary funding source, supplemented by debt expansion (growing the debt portfolio from ~$16 billion to ~$100 billion over the past 12 months).
  - Equity was raised recently to maintain a resilient balance sheet, though Alphabet does not plan to return to equity markets outside of an "at-the-market" (ATM) offering dedicated to covering stock-based compensation taxes.

## Google Cloud & Infrastructure Momentum
- **Segment Results:** 
  - Cloud revenue surged **82% to $24.8 billion**, with core GCP growing faster than the Cloud overall.
  - Cloud operating income more than tripled year-over-year to **$8.8 billion**, with operating margin expanding from 20.7% to **35.6%**.
  - Google Cloud backlog increased by over $50 billion sequentially to **$514 billion**, with just over 50% expected to be recognized as revenue over the next 24 months.
- **Enterprise & Token Adoption:**
  - Nearly **90% of Fortune 100** companies use Gemini Enterprise.
  - Nearly **500 cloud customers** each processed more than 1 trillion tokens in the last year; over 2,000 enterprises consumed over 100 billion tokens over the last 12 months.
  - **Gemini Enterprise Adoption:** Agent Development Kit reached nearly **70 million total downloads** in Q2. Named customers include PepsiCo, Intel, HSBC, Bell Canada, Macy's, and Signal Aduna.
- **AI Infrastructure & Hardware:**
  - Broad range of accelerators offered, including Google TPUs (AT and ATI) and Nvidia platforms (including the new Nvidia Verarummin platform).
  - **Virgo Network:** Connects a million AI accelerators across multiple data center sites into a unified supercomputer.
  - **Axion CPU:** Agent-optimized CPU providing 30% better performance per dollar compared to peer offerings.
  - **TPU System Sales:** Alphabet began recognizing revenues from TPU system deliveries to customer data centers in Q2.

## Google Services & Search Performance
- **Segment Results:** 
  - Google Services revenues rose **15% to $94.5 billion**.
  - Search and other advertising revenues grew **17% to $63.3 billion**, led by retail and finance.
  - YouTube advertising revenues increased **13% to $11.1 billion**, driven by direct response and brand advertising.
  - Network advertising revenues fell **1% to $7.3 billion**.
  - Subscription, platforms, and devices revenues increased **15% to $12.9 billion**, driven by YouTube subscriptions (Music and Premium) and Google One (AI plans).
- **Search & AI Integration:**
  - AI mode surpassed **1 billion monthly active users** globally since its launch last October, driving incremental search queries and billions of weekly clicks to websites.
  - AI overviews and AI mode were combined into one seamless search experience.
  - Gemini-powered shopping ads drove a **20% improvement** in showing highly relevant ads.
  - Cost of AI mode responses was reduced to its lowest level since launch.
- **YouTube Scale & Monetization:**
  - FIFA World Cup 2026 became the most-viewed World Cup in YouTube history, with over **1.7 billion unique viewers** globally watching related videos, and over 550 million watching on televisions.
  - **Ask YouTube:** Over **140 million users** engaged with conversational AI summaries on the watch page in June 2026.
  - YouTube subscriptions are growing faster than ads, led by YouTube Music and Premium.

## Ecosystem, Developers, & Other Bets
- **Model Ecosystem & Developer Traction:**
  - Released Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flashlight, and 3.5 Flash Cyber (paired with code mender agent). Pre-training has begun for the ambitious **Gemini 4** base model.
  - Model APIs are processing approximately **22 billion tokens per minute** (up from 16 billion last quarter). Over **9 million developers** build each month.
  - **Jemma Family:** Open models downloaded over 900 million times total, with latest Jemma 4 models downloaded over 300 million times since April.
  - **Antigravity:** Agentic development platform with over **2.4 million weekly active users**.
  - **Gemini App:** Reached **950 million monthly active users**, with daily active users tripling over the last year. Daily video-creation active users on the app increased 40% since May.
- **Ads & Commerce Tools:**
  - **AI Max:** Adopted by **half a million advertisers**, delivering an average of 15% more conversions or value on search at a similar ROAS. Triple A Autoclop Enterprises saw a 17% conversion volume improvement and 11% cost-per-lead decrease using AI Max.
  - Over half of global SMB customers use AI to create or optimize ad creatives.
- **Other Bets:**
  - **Waymo:** Introduced the newest vehicle, OHA, to public riders, powered by the sixth-generation Waymo driver.
  - **Wing:** Safely completed over **1 million home deliveries** through partnerships with Walmart, DoorDash, and Papa Johns.
  - **Isomorphic Labs:** Raised over **$2 billion** to power its AI drug design engine.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Anat Ashkenazi (CFO) / Sundar Pichai (CEO) on CapEx Guidance:** Alphabet updated its full-year 2026 CapEx guidance range to **$195 billion to $205 billion** (up from the previous estimate of $180 billion to $190 billion), driven by an acceleration in capacity delivery. CapEx is expected to increase significantly further in 2027.
- **Anat Ashkenazi (CFO) on Q3 Revenue FX & Growth Lapping:** At current spot rates, a slight foreign exchange headwind is expected for consolidated revenue in Q3 (compared to a 1 percentage point tailwind in Q2), impacting Search and YouTube ads primarily. In Q3, Alphabet will also begin lapping an acceleration in Search performance that began in Q3 of the prior year.
- **Anat Ashkenazi (CFO) on TPU Revenue Recognition:** A relatively small portion of revenues from existing TPU system sales agreements will be recognized in 2026, ramping as the company exits 2026, with the vast majority of revenues realized in **2027**.
- **Anat Ashkenazi (CFO) on Cloud Margin Pressures:** Due to supply constraints, Alphabet plans to expand the use of third-party capacity in Q3 as a bridging strategy, which will create modest near-term margin pressure for Google Cloud. Near-term P&L pressure will also persist from higher depreciation and energy costs, ongoing hiring in AI and Cloud, marketing investments, and the integration headwinds from the Wiz acquisition in 2026.
- **Anat Ashkenazi (CFO) on Cloud Backlog Realization:** Just over **50% of the total $514 billion cloud backlog** is expected to be recognized as revenue over the next **24 months**.
- **Anat Ashkenazi (CFO) on ATM Equity Offerings:** Alphabet does not plan to return to the equity markets for funding, with the sole exception of continuing its at-the-market (ATM) equity offering for some period of time to address the tax obligations on stock-based compensation (SBC).

## Notable Quotes
> "We've started our most ambitious pre-training run yet for Gemini 4 and are excited by the progress we are seeing at the frontier." - Sundar Pichai on model development
> 
> "Our cloud backlog grew to $514 billion... Just over 50% of the total backlog [is expected] as revenue over the next 24 months." - Sundar Pichai and Anat Ashkenazi on cloud demand
> 
> "We are updating our full-year 2026 CAPEX guidance range to $195 to $205 billion, up from our previous estimate of $180 to $190 billion." - Anat Ashkenazi on capital expenditure acceleration

briefings.title: BIG BET: Cathie Wood goes ALL IN on Elon Musk
briefings.tldr: ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood and guest experts on Mornings with Maria discuss how AI, aerospace, and autonomous defense technologies are driving a once-in-a-generation productivity boom and reshaping global competition with China.
briefings.summary_markdown:
- **TL;DR:** ARK Invest CEO Cathie Wood and guest experts on *Mornings with Maria* discuss how AI, aerospace, and autonomous defense technologies are driving a once-in-a-generation productivity boom and reshaping global competition with China.
- Wood argues that SpaceX—leveraging a 10-year lead in reusable rockets, a 70% share of satellites, and upcoming orbital data centers—is positioned to become the most important company in global history.

## AI Infrastructure, Productivity, and the U.S.–China Race
- **Macroeconomic Productivity:** 
  - Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent notes that the current AI build-up is a once-in-a-generation driver of natural wealth through productivity growth.
  - The administration supports open-source models but warns against IP theft, retaining the ability to sanction overseas models caught stealing from U.S. companies.
- **Assessing Chinese AI Competitors:**
  - Cathie Wood views the competition positively, noting that America is at its best when competing.
  - **DeepSeek & Communiqué Analysis:** ARK's research indicates that Chinese models are less expensive upfront but much less efficient, relying on "throwing power at the AI equation."
- **Wall Street AI Adoption (BNY Mellon):**
  - BNY CEO Robin Vince reports that the bank built its own platform named **Eliza** (after Alexander Hamilton's spouse) with internal agent builders.
  - The bank has conducted 10 to 40 hours of training per employee and currently has **200 solutions in production**.

## SpaceX: Dominating Aerospace, Telecom, and Data
- **Market Valuation and Holdings:** 
  - ARK Invest manages **$30 billion** in total assets.
  - SpaceX is trading below its peak (down 32% in the past month), with **$116 billion** in shares set to unlock following the lifting of IPO restrictions.
  - Wood’s firm has increased exposure by **$80 million** since the IPO.
- **Competitive Advantage:**
  - **Launch Capabilities & Reusability:** SpaceX holds a **10-year lead**, anchored by its pioneering work in landing and relaunching rockets. While Blue Origin successfully landed a rocket late last year, it did not successfully relaunch it into orbit in the desired manner.
  - **Global Telecom Disruption:** Telecom has historically been a local business requiring the purchase of domestic telcos. SpaceX bypasses this with a global network, holding **70% of all satellites**.
  - **Orbital Data Centers:** SpaceX is building global data centers in orbit and currently rents out terrestrial data centers to companies like **Anthropic** and **Google**.
  - **Long-Term Strategy:** While making short-term deals with terrestrial telcos (like AT&T), SpaceX ultimately plans to go direct-to-business globally at lower costs.

## AI Disruption in Healthcare and Corporate America
- **Corporate Productivity & Talent:**
  - Companies are heavily investing in AI for internal and customer-facing workflows.
  - ARK leverages tools like Palantir and actively recruits young, AI-native talent, viewing the technology as a fundamental mindset shift.
- **Healthcare Transformation:**
  - Wood highlights healthcare as the most profound application of AI due to the convergence of **three technologies**: AI drug discovery (collapsing time and cost), predictive diagnostics (identifying diseases before symptoms appear via sequencing), and **CRISPR gene editing**.

## Defense Technology and Manufacturing Leapfrogging
- **Autonomous Maritime and Defense (Ceronix):**
  - Ceronix CEO Dino argues that the U.S. does not need to beat China by building traditional 1,200-foot cargo containers or matching legacy shipyards (Port Alpha).
  - Instead, the U.S. will win by out-producing China through **autonomous vessels**, software platforms, efficient new shipyards, and asymmetric capabilities controlled by software.
- **Leapfrogging Old Technology:**
  - Wood compares current manufacturing shifts to how China previously leaped over U.S. infrastructure—adopting wireless directly instead of building landlines, and digital wallets instead of brick-and-mortar banking. 
  - The U.S. can similarly leapfrog legacy industrial approaches through autonomous, software-driven manufacturing.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **SpaceX's Historical Trajectory:** Cathie Wood predicts that SpaceX could become "the most important company in global history" by combining launch capabilities, global communications, the robotaxi opportunity, orbital data centers, and frontier models (including xAI/Optimist).
- **Multi-Trillion Dollar Opportunities:** Cathie Wood predicts that the convergence of robotics, AI models, and space infrastructure will create "multi-trillion dollar opportunities."

## Notable Quotes
> *"We think this could be possible, the most important company in global history and I mean in global history because we are talking about not only exploring a new world... but also a global communications network."* — **Cathie Wood**

> *"We don't have to beat China in the traditional sense of let's go out build what they are building. We are going to beat China in a new way, out produce China by building autonomous vessels..."* — **Dino (Ceronix CEO)**

> *"It's a superpowerful technology... We've got 200 solutions in production and we really believe AI can be a superpower for the company and a superpower for the people in the company."* — **Robin Vince (BNY CEO)**

briefings.title: Building a Company in Stealth | Travis Kalanick with a16z
briefings.tldr: Travis Kalanick, Ben Horowitz, and Erik Torenberg reflect on Uber's legendary early days, the 2011 Series B investment that nearly happened with a16z, and Kalanick's 8-year stealth return building Atoms—a company digitizing the physical world across food, mining, and autonomous transport using industrial AI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Travis Kalanick, Ben Horowitz, and Erik Torenberg reflect on Uber's legendary early days, the 2011 Series B investment that nearly happened with a16z, and Kalanick's 8-year stealth return building Atoms—a company digitizing the physical world across food, mining, and autonomous transport using industrial AI.

## The Deal That Got Away: Uber's Series B (2011)
* **The A16Z Pitch and Breakdown:** Travis Kalanick describes running a high-momentum "winner takes all" auction for Uber's Series B in 2011, securing an uncapped anchor at a $375M pre-money valuation with a16z. Ben Horowitz explains that after the pitch, he passed the deal to Mark and John O'Ferrell, but the partnership backed off the $375M price tag, counter-offering $210M—collapsing Kalanick's momentum and forcing him to restart the auction.
* **The Butterfly Effect:** Horowitz and Kalanick both agree that if a16z had been on Uber's board in 2011, the company's tumultuous 2017 would have been avoided, and Uber would be significantly larger today, likely dominating food delivery and autonomy outright. 
* **The Lift Parallel:** Horowitz shares that a16z subsequently backed Lyft, a competitive startup that launched into extreme difficulties largely because of Uber, eventually forcing Horowitz to take a board seat to help steady it.

## The Evolution of Leadership: From Pirate to Navy
* **Managing Growth and Governance:** Reflecting on his 2017 departure from Uber, Kalanick notes that while he stands by every decision, he pushed too close to the line and failed to realize that big enterprises must transition from an upstart "pirate" mentality to a disciplined "navy" framework.
* **Aggressive Tactics:** Kalanick shares that internal programs like "shoplifting" (aggressively recruiting drivers away from Lyft) had to be rebranded to harmless names like the North American Championship Series (NACS) after pushback from board members like David Drummond and legal training on antitrust rules.
* **Post-Uber Hell:** Kalanick spent 7-8 months post-Uber fighting lawsuits and investigations before finding his next venture.

## Building in Stealth: The 8-Year Journey of Atoms
* **Origins as Cloud Kitchens:** Following his exit from Uber, Kalanick partnered with a real estate savant who had started Cloud Kitchens (originally incorporated as City Storage Systems), a multi-tenant delivery-only commercial kitchen concept. Kalanick acquired the company and scaled it into a global operation.
* **Operating in Hard Mode:** To escape the 150 negative media articles a day from his final days at Uber, Kalanick operated in strict stealth for nearly 8 years, growing to thousands of employees across 30 countries (operating under various local names like Kitchen Valley in Korea, Flash Kitchen in China, and Food Stars in London) without the New York Times knowing.
* **The Cultural Advantage of Stealth:** Operating in stealth starved the company of external validation and fame-seeking, forcing internal correctness, emotional intelligence, and genuine fulfillment from the daily work rather than press clippings.

## Digitizing the Physical World: The Atoms-Based Computer
* **The Atoms Framework:** Kalanick explains his thesis that physical world industries can be modeled using computer science architecture: 
  * **Manufacturing** = CPU (manipulates atoms)
  * **Real Estate** = Storage (stores atoms)
  * **Transport & Logistics** = Network (moves atoms)
* **The Food Computer Vision:** The ultimate goal for Atoms Food is to make the preparation and delivery of a quality meal so efficient that it approaches the grocery store cost, effectively doing to the kitchen what Uber did to the car. This requires automated manufacturing (food robotics) and robotic couriers to drop distribution costs from $12 per meal down to $0.50–$1.00.
* **Expanding into Mining (Pronto):** Atoms acquired Pronto, an off-road autonomy and mining automation company where Kalanick was an early investor. The business targets a 20% increase in productivity and critical safety improvements for gold and mineral mines globally.

## Industrial AI and the Future of Physical Automation
* **Industrial AI Stack:** Kalanick defines the emerging category of Industrial AI as a practical stack of software, sensors, robotics, and machinery designed to automate heavy, multi-trillion-dollar physical industries one at a time—starting with food, mining, and transport.
* **Parallels to the Second Industrial Revolution:** Horowitz and Kalanick draw strong parallels between today's regulatory and public resistance to physical AI, data centers, and industrial automation and the struggles faced by historical industrialists like Carnegie, Rockefeller, and Ford.

## Notable Quotes
> "The meaningful thing about Atoms food... can you make the preparation and delivery of a quality meal so efficient that it approaches the cost of going to the grocery store? If it does, you do to the kitchen what Uber did to the car."
> — Travis Kalanick

> "When you fall in love again, you don't think about the ex very much."
> — Travis Kalanick

> "He's one of the very rare guys who made as much money as he did and wanted to keep playing... There's only one non-fungible, very rare person in that equation who could do that."
> — Ben Horowitz (on Travis Kalanick)

> "Everybody loves progress. It's change they can't stand."
> — Ben Horowitz

briefings.title: Fireside Chat with Sid Sheth, Founder & CEO of d-Matrix | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Sid Sheth and Tony Kim discuss how d-Matrix's purpose-built inference hardware—transitioning from SRAM-based accelerators to 3D-stacked DRAM-on-compute architectures—addresses the unique demands of the agentic AI era by optimizing for interactivity and energy efficiency.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Sid Sheth and Tony Kim discuss how d-Matrix's purpose-built inference hardware—transitioning from SRAM-based accelerators to 3D-stacked DRAM-on-compute architectures—addresses the unique demands of the agentic AI era by optimizing for interactivity and energy efficiency.

## Company Overview & Market Positioning
* **Company Background:** Founded in 2019 by Sid Sheth, d-Matrix is a chip company focused entirely on AI inference, operating in a capital-intensive sector for seven years.
* **Current Status:** d-Matrix has announced that its products are officially moving into production and are ready for deployment.
* **The Inference Thesis:** Analogous to human development (spending 20+ years learning vs. 40+ years applying knowledge), inference represents a vastly larger and more economically critical market opportunity than training.
* **Optimization Metrics:** Unlike training (which prioritizes raw performance, data scale, and cluster throughput), inference prioritizes efficiency metrics:
  * Speed: Milliseconds per token
  * Cost: Dollars per token
  * Energy: Throughput per watt and interactivity limits

## Architectural Approaches: SRAM vs. HBM
* **The X-Axis vs. Y-Axis Trade-off:** 
  * *Y-Axis (HBM/GPUs):* Optimized for throughput and batching multiple users, but struggles with extreme speed/interactivity.
  * *X-Axis (SRAM/d-Matrix):* Optimized for speed, low energy consumption, and high interactivity through in-memory compute (minimizing data movement).
* **The SRAM Capacity Constraint:** Pure SRAM architectures (like those from Grock, Cerebras, and d-Matrix) face capacity challenges with very large models or long context lengths.
* **Heterogeneous Disaggregated Computing:** 
  * Workloads are split by running the compute-heavy prefill portion on HBM GPUs and memory-intensive token generation on SRAM accelerators.
  * d-Matrix announced a partnership with NVIDIA for a target customer called Parasale (an inference cloud) combining Blackwell GPUs with d-Matrix Corsair SRAM accelerators.

## The Next Generation: 3D-Stacked DRAM
* **The Architectural "Endgame":** To overcome SRAM capacity limits without sacrificing speed, d-Matrix is building a "skyscraper" architecture by stacking custom DRAM directly on top of SRAM compute layers, rather than placing memory to the side like HBM.
* **Scaling Layers:** d-Matrix's roadmap starts with 1 layer of memory in their next-generation product, scaling to 4 layers, and eventually 8 layers (comparable to HBM stack heights).
* **Bridging the Axes:** This stacked approach allows d-Matrix to maintain deep X-axis interactivity while shifting upward on the Y-axis by expanding capacity for more users and larger context lengths.
* **Market Coexistence:** GPU-based HBM solutions and stacked-DRAM/SRAM solutions will coexist because frontier models trained on GPUs will continue to require GPU-level capabilities, while cost- and power-conscious deployments will utilize disaggregated architectures.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Sid Sheth:** d-Matrix's production version of its 3D-stacked DRAM product will tape out and come to market in **2027**, making them "amongst the first companies to release a product of that type."

## Notable Quotes
> "Training AI is, you know, very similar to training humans. We spent the first, you know, 20 years of our life going to, you know, school and college. But then we spend 40 plus years applying that knowledge... inference was the much larger opportunity compared to training because everyone needs to use it."
> — **Sid Sheth**

> "When you're trying to do more work, it typically needs more time... And most HBM based solutions today fall on that Y-axis... On the X-axis is speed; you fundamentally need a different type of memory hierarchy to address that piece of the equation."
> — **Sid Sheth**

briefings.title: Keynote by Maor Shlomo, Founder & CEO of Base44 | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Base44, an 18-month-old vibe coding platform, scaled to over $150 million in ARR with zero outside capital by operating primarily as a one-person team leveraging AI agents—leading to its recent acquisition by Wix.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Base44, an 18-month-old vibe coding platform, scaled to over $150 million in ARR with zero outside capital by operating primarily as a one-person team leveraging AI agents—leading to its recent acquisition by Wix. Founder & CEO Maor Shlomo attributes this hyper-growth to organizational restructuring around "teams of one," a strict 30% rule for building internal tools, and compounding ambitions.

## Company Background & Growth Metrics
* **Base44 Metrics:**
  * **Age:** 18 months old
  * **Revenue:** Over $150 million in ARR
  * **Funding:** $0 raised from investors
  * **Growth Rate:** Grew 50x over the past year
  * **Team Structure:** For most of its existence, operated as a one-person company (Maor Shlomo plus agents handling engineering, marketing, and support)
  * **Exit:** Recently acquired by Wix
  * **Execution Speed:** Pushes code to production hundreds of times a day; has 41 direct reports reporting to the CEO; manages end-to-end billing with a single person

* **Origin Story:**
  * Started as a casual experiment by Maor Shlomo to see how far he could push AI development without following traditional startup playbooks
  * Named "Base44" after cycling through numbers to find an available domain name when base.com was taken
  * **Previous Venture:** Shlomo co-founded Explorium eight years prior, which followed the traditional VC playbook of heavy hiring, layers of management, and functional silos (product, design, engineering)
  * **The ChatGPT Disruption:** The 2023 shift to LLMs broke Explorium's traditional market; the traditional multi-layered corporate structure proved too slow to pivot effectively, prompting Shlomo's post-burnout realization that the old startup playbook was obsolete

## Organizational Structure: Teams of One
* **Individual Conductors (ICs):** 
  * Traditional ICs ("individual contributors") have been redefined as "individual conductors" who partner with AI agents to deliver end-to-end value without cross-team dependencies
* **Flat and Lean Scaling:**
  * Base44 avoids management layers, communication bottlenecks, and traditional communication friction
  * Mirrors broader industry trends where top research labs pay hundreds of millions of dollars for outlier individuals rather than assembling massive engineering headcounts

## The 30% Rule & Working on Working
* **Reinvesting Time:** 
  * 30% of the team's time is reinvested directly into building custom tools, automations, and agents that accelerate workflows
* **Exponential Productivity:** 
  * Rather than relying on generic software that competitors also use, Base44 builds personalized tools on its own vibe coding platform tailored specifically to its operational bottlenecks
* **Custom Tooling Examples:**
  * Built proprietary task management platforms optimized for daily-only meetings (Base44 maintains a strict "no meetings" policy outside of a single morning check-in)
  * Developed custom tools for managing experiments, production agents, content writing, and enterprise sales/go-to-market agents

## Compounding Ambitions
* **Mindset Shift:** 
  * AI dramatically increases operational throughput, meaning leadership must recalibrate how ambitious their product roadmap can be instead of merely executing the same backlog faster
* **Recent Output Highlights:**
  * Trained and released a proprietary LLM within a few months
  * Launched a mobile app for Base44
  * Extended capabilities to website games, presentation slides, agents, and automations

## Notable Quotes
> "I tried everything. We had to go back to being a very lean startup mode... And this was a company that just followed the right playbook, the playbook of how to build a startup before 2023."
> — *Maor Shlomo*

> "Before the age of AI, we were building companies to be efficient teams that communicate well and have the right structure. I think now everything is changing. I think now the way I like it to look at organizations is we should build them around teams of one."
> — *Maor Shlomo*

> "Every day there's like a new stuff, but I think the key thing that unlocked our own productivity is looking at our own bottlenecks and understanding what are the things that we should build customized solutions for that are going to accelerate 10x than the existing solutions."
> — *Maor Shlomo*

briefings.title: NVIDIA & Wistron: Reindustrializing America With Advanced Manufacturing
briefings.tldr: Jensen Huang and Simon Lin discuss how the buildout of AI supercomputers and factories—such as Wistron's new Fort Worth facility producing NVIDIA GB300 and Vera Rubin chips—is driving a multi-trillion-dollar reindustrialization of the United States.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Jensen Huang and Simon Lin discuss how the buildout of AI supercomputers and factories—such as Wistron's new Fort Worth facility producing NVIDIA GB300 and Vera Rubin chips—is driving a multi-trillion-dollar reindustrialization of the United States.

## AI Infrastructure and Advanced Manufacturing
- **Wistron's U.S. Facility:** Producing the NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Superchip and will produce the NVIDIA Vera Rubin Superchip in Fort Worth, Texas.
- **Scale of the GB300 Supercomputer:** 
  - Contains **1.5 million parts**
  - Weighs **2 tons**
  - Priced at **$4 million**
- **Reindustrialization Impact:** U.S. manufacturing has added several million jobs over the past couple of years across construction, plumbing, electricians, chip plants, packaging plants, computer system plants, and AI data centers/factories.
- **Supply Chain Integration:** Taiwan serves as NVIDIA's largest trading partner and a vital supplier for building resilient U.S. manufacturing capacity alongside partners like TSMC and Wistron.

## Generative Computing vs. Retrieval Computing
- **Shift to Generative Models:** Traditional data centers stored pre-recorded information (photos, videos, files) for retrieval. Modern AI "factories" process generative models that reason, write stories, generate images, create tables, and produce answers dynamically.
- **The "Token" Economy:** 
  - AI factories manufacture trillions of tokens (numbers that translate into words, poetry, images, and songs).
  - Huang compares the economic value of digital tokens to entertainment spending (e.g., a $24.99 movie translating to billions of tokens).
- **Chip Demand Surge:** The transition from retrieval computing (growing at **25% per year**) to generative computing supercomputers has increased chip demand by roughly **10x**.

## Industrial Transformation and the New CAPEX Layer
- **Energy and Sustainability:** 
  - AI is a major driver for the energy industry, enabling sustainable energy investment and power grid upgrades without government subsidies.
  - Modern AI factories are energy efficient, using closed-loop liquid cooling systems that recirculate water (using roughly the water of a swimming pool with no loss).
- **Every Company as a Technology Company:** 
  - Industries traditionally characterized by low CAPEX (such as law firms) will transition to higher CAPEX models combining human intelligence (coffee and hamburgers) with digital intelligence (electricity and tokens).
- **Societal Infrastructure:** AI factories will become foundational infrastructure akin to roads, railroads, and agriculture, generating a new layer of economic activity valued in the **trillions of dollars**.

## National and Corporate Sovereignty in AI
- **Sovereign Intelligence:** Huang argues that no country, company, or society can outsource its culture, intelligence, or knowledge.
- **Model Diversity:** Societies should utilize off-the-shelf closed models for general tasks while cultivating their own open and closed models to preserve national and corporate intelligence.

## Notable Quotes
> "Without the partnership of Taiwan, without the partnership of TSMC and Wistron, uh we wouldn't be able to do what we are doing today. So so for that, I'm incredibly grateful." — **Jensen Huang**

> "This is the first time in human history where we could invest in sustainable energy without contribution from the government, without subsidies, because the market dynamic would itself would invest in sustainable energy." — **Jensen Huang**

> "No country can outsource its intelligence. No company can outsource all of its intelligence. No society can outsource its culture." — **Jensen Huang**

briefings.title: Pat Gelsinger & Elad Raz: Where Chips Go After the GPU Era | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: As AI workloads evolve rapidly beyond standard transformers toward agentic, continuous-learning, and multi-dimensional physical models, fixed ASICs face obsolescence, necessitating software-driven, flexible architectures that can balance high-performance computing (HPC) and AI on a unified chip.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
As AI workloads evolve rapidly beyond standard transformers toward agentic, continuous-learning, and multi-dimensional physical models, fixed ASICs face obsolescence, necessitating software-driven, flexible architectures that can balance high-performance computing (HPC) and AI on a unified chip.

## The Convergence of HPC and AI Workloads
* **Unified Mathematical Principles:** 
  * **Elad Raz:** Emphasizes that at their foundation, HPC (fluid dynamics, security, defense, physical simulation) and AI share identical mathematical principles, with AI workloads actually being simpler.
  * **Shared Code Execution:** NextSilicon’s Maverick accelerator was designed with a data-flow architecture for parallel code sections, complemented by an integrated RISC-V CPU to accelerate serial code.
* **Legacy Compatibility:** 
  * **Diverse Software Support:** NextSilicon's architecture is agnostic to MLOps frameworks, running code written in Triton, CUDA, C, PyTorch, and even legacy Fortran used extensively in supercomputing and scientific workloads.

## The Renaissance of the CPU in the AI Era
* **Shifting Compute Ratios:** 
  * **Pat Gelsinger:** Notes that historical CPU-to-GPU ratios (1 CPU to 8 or 16 GPUs) are shifting toward 1-to-2 or even 1-to-1 ratios to handle agentic multi-model environments and workload affinity.
* **Workload-Driven Design:** 
  * **Architecture Follows Function:** Gelsinger stresses that computing has never been about underlying architecture, but rather how workloads are executed across the software-hardware stack.
* **Agentic Tools Integration:** 
  * **Elad Raz:** Points out that as LLMs execute tasks using multiple agentic tools and generate codebases for physical simulations, local memory retention on a single chip running both AI and physical simulation is critical.

## The Flaws of Specialized ASICs and Fixed Architectures
* **The Danger of Single-Purpose Chips:** 
  * **Elad Raz:** Criticizes the trend of building custom ASICs exclusively for specific architectures (such as the Llama transformer), noting that rapid innovations in MLOps—like attention heads, multi-latent attention, sparse attention, and Mamba models operating in frequency space—render single-purpose hardware obsolete.
* **Absorbed Specialization:** 
  * **Pat Gelsinger:** Draws historical parallels to floating-point and media processors, which initially emerged as specialized units before being absorbed into general machine architecture as workloads evolved.
* **Avoiding Compute Islands:** 
  * Carving workloads up into isolated specialized zones (such as splitting training farms from pre-fill and decode) creates unscalable "islands of compute."

## NextSilicon’s Architecture and Industry Validation
* **Development Milestones:** 
  * **Elad Raz:** Reports that NextSilicon spent 8 years and completed 4 tape-outs. Their first generation is deployed in national laboratories, and their second generation is in production and installed at the rack level with Department of Energy (DOE) entities.
* **The Arbel RISC-V Spin-Off:** 
  * Spun off their internal RISC-V chip (named Arbel) from the Maverick accelerator to create a best-in-class silicon core for high-performance serial code execution alongside data-flow parallel acceleration.
* **Capital and Innovation Costs:** 
  * **Elad Raz:** Notes that every chip generation costs approximately $150 million to develop, requiring distinct architectural advantages and early testing with scale customers.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Architectural Agnosticism Requirement:** **Elad Raz** states that because chip design takes 3 years and future models cannot be accurately predicted, hardware must be built as an architecture capable of accelerating whatever comes next.
* **Evolution of AI Models:** **Pat Gelsinger** predicts that models will transition from today's two-dimensional transformers into three- and four-dimensional models to accommodate molecular structures and physical AI.
* **Decaying Boundaries:** **Pat Gelsinger** predicts the boundary between training and inferencing will decay over time, giving rise to algorithms that enable continuous self-training.
* **The 10,000x Efficiency Target:** **Pat Gelsinger** asserts that computing infrastructure must become 10,000 times better to make AI energy- and capital-efficient enough to support next-generation chemistry, biology, material science, and human-centric computing, potentially incorporating technologies like cryogenic computing.

## Notable Quotes
> "Anybody that can predict the AI future 2 years from now is lying. It's just dynamically changing so rapidly associated with it."
> — **Pat Gelsinger**

> "We have to make AI 10,000 times better than today, right? It isn't going to be a little bit better, we need to make it 10,000x, it is much too energy inefficient, much too capital, uh, inefficient if we're fully going to realize the benefits of AI for humanity's future."
> — **Pat Gelsinger**

> "Chip design takes 3 years, so you need to predict which model will run 3 years from now. You can't do that, so build an architecture that whatever comes next, you can accelerate."
> — **Elad Raz**

briefings.title: Sovereign AI: Piece by Piece | NetApp, Radiant, Hydra Host, Coatue & More | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Sovereign AI is emerging as a critical, multi-layered geopolitical trend where nations and enterprises seek independent control over their AI infrastructure, data, and operations.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Sovereign AI is emerging as a critical, multi-layered geopolitical trend where nations and enterprises seek independent control over their AI infrastructure, data, and operations. While the U.S. and China are building dominant full-stack ecosystems, other regions like Europe, Latin America, and Asia are navigating complex trade-offs between local control, cost, and the realities of global supply chain dependencies.

## Definitions & Core Concepts of Sovereign AI
*   **National and Organizational Control:** George Kurian (NetApp) defines Sovereign AI as the ability of a nation-state or organization to independently control the development, deployment, and governance of AI activities, encompassing technology, data, operations, and talent.
*   **A Continuous Spectrum:** Mahdi Yahya (Radiant) emphasizes that sovereignty is not a binary end state, but a continuous spectrum where organizations constantly make decisions on how much control to exert and how much risk to divest.
*   **Data Residency and Physical Infrastructure:** Aaron Ginn (Hydra Host) argues that sovereignty starts with data residency, physical data center infrastructure, and local retention of chips and capital rather than relying on foreign hyperscalers.
*   **Critical Infrastructure & Utility:** Ben Germin (Polarise) frames AI tokens as a critical utility comparable to gas, water, and electricity, making it vital for Europe to avoid dependency on hyperscalers and the U.S. Cloud Act.
*   **Data Ownership & Open Models:** Max Cook (Coatue) highlights that enterprise sovereignty also means owning proprietary data and managing whether open versus closed models are utilized.

## The AI Technology Stack and Supply Chain Realities
*   **Control Planes as Critical Control Points:** Mahdi Yahya states that controlling the management plane above and below physical infrastructure is the most critical element of the Sovereign AI stack.
*   **The Power Bottleneck:** Max Cook points out that upstream equipment bottlenecks—such as gas turbines used for power generation (dominated by just three global suppliers, one American)—heavily dictate where infrastructure can be built, with much equipment still flowing to the U.S.
*   **Data Control as a Durable Moat:** George Kurian notes that NetApp works to give clients complete control to deploy data anywhere—whether hyperscaler, sovereign environment, or on-premises data center.
*   **Decentralized OS and Global Deployments:** Aaron Ginn shares that Hydra Host provides data center-level OS layers for sovereign clients, telecom firms, and energy companies, enabling them to run NVIDIA hardware without in-house expertise across diverse locations like El Salvador and Panama.
*   **The Impact of Export Controls:** George Kurian notes that U.S. export controls have spurred innovation, forcing China to develop diffusion-based models and encouraging global competition.

## Hyperscalers vs. Independent Infrastructure
*   **The Infeasibility of Hyperscalers for True Sovereignty:** Ben Germin offers a clear "no" on achieving true sovereignty via hyperscalers, citing Microsoft France's legal testimony before the French Senate that it cannot guarantee data stays within France.
*   **The Three Phases of Government Action:** Mahdi Yahya outlines that governments move through *rhetoric, policy,* and finally *execution*, noting that most governments have not yet reached the execution phase.
*   **Commercial Risk vs. National Security:** George Kurian distinguishes between commercial organizations prioritizing intellectual property protection and risk, and governments balancing national security with the need to foster local ecosystems and innovation.

## The Economic Cost and Inelasticity of Sovereign AI
*   **Financial Duplication:** Max Cook and George Kurian note that building sovereign AI requires duplicating data center infrastructure and procuring more semiconductors, which inherently increases costs.
*   **Token Price Deflation and Margins:** Ben Germin notes that while building AI factories in Munich and Oslo is expensive, token prices are deflationary, leaving sufficient margin across different layers to remain profitable and competitive.
*   **Inelastic Demand for Intelligence:** Aaron Ginn argues that Sovereign AI is economically inelastic because intelligence is unbounded and governments view *not* having it as a greater risk than any financial cost.

## Regional Progress and Global Execution
*   **Latin America & El Salvador:** Aaron Ginn highlights projects with the President of El Salvador, building Latin America's first black hole data center deployment, alongside massive power capacity in Paraguay (3 gigawatts).
*   **France & Europe:** Mahdi Yahya notes Brookfield Asset Management commitments, including $30 billion in France and investments in Sweden. Ben Germin details a 10-megawatt AI industry cloud deployment in Germany with Telekom that expanded Germany's AI compute by 50%.
*   **Asia:** Aaron Ginn notes that China's top models grew from 10% to over 50% of the global top tier, creating an independent eastern ecosystem.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
*   **Silicon Independence Timeline:** George Kurian predicts that it is "inconceivable" that silicon competitive with U.S. silicon will emerge within the next 5 years.
*   **Global Ecosystem Bifurcation (5-Year Outlook):** George Kurian predicts that in 5 years, the U.S. will maintain the full stack (chips to apps), while China will establish a robust alternative ecosystem anchored by open-source models and a coalition of adopting nations.
*   **Airline Industry Parallel:** Aaron Ginn predicts that GPUs and models will ultimately mirror the commercial airline industry, where a couple of dominant global players (like Airbus and Boeing) exist alongside numerous local and regional carrier providers reflecting local resources.
*   **Persistent European Dependency:** Ben Germin predicts that in 5 years, Europe will still remain heavily dependent on hyperscalers for infrastructure, foreign chips, and foreign foundation models, despite the rise of local star initiatives.

## Notable Quotes
> "Governments today... go through three phases, there's rhetoric, then there is policy and then there is execution. I don't think we got to the execution phase yet, in any of the different governments."
> — **Mahdi Yahya**

> "GPUs are regulated on the US government as if it is a missile defense technology... Once the government's decide that something is regulated that way, it does it generally doesn't go the other way."
> — **Aaron Ginn**

> "We have to come with a gun to the gunfight in the end, not with a knife."
> — **Ben Germin**

> "Constraints usually create innovation... It fosters different ecosystems. It brings lower cost models into play. It creates alternate chip designs and all of those things."
> — **George Kurian**

briefings.title: Tesla Q2 2026 Financial Results and Q&A Webcast

briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Tesla reported record Q2 2026 vehicle deliveries and a massive 53% sequential increase in energy storage deployments (13.5 GWh), driven by surging demand for Full Self-Driving (FSD) and energy infrastructure, even as capital expenditures doubled to over $25 billion annualized and operating expenses rose due to R&D for Robotaxi, Optimus, and AI chips.

## Financial Results & Business Performance
*   **Automotive Metrics:** 
    *   Achieved record Q2 deliveries with sequential growth across the Americas (60%), APAC (27%), and EMEA (12%), exiting the quarter with the largest order backlog since 2023.
    *   Model Y set records in key markets including the Netherlands, Australia, and New Zealand.
    *   Automotive gross margins (excluding regulatory credits) declined sequentially from 19.2% to 16.3%, impacted by higher interest rate subvention costs and the non-repetition of Q1 warranty true-downs ($230M) and tariff benefits — **Vaibhav Taneja**
*   **Energy Storage Business:** 
    *   Deployed 13.5 GWh of energy storage in Q2 (a 53% sequential increase), marking the second-largest quarter in the business's history — **Vaibhav Taneja**
    *   Energy gross margins dropped from 39.5% to 20.4% due to a $240M legacy vendor cell warranty true-up, the absence of Q1 tariff benefits ($200M+), and declining industrial storage ASPs amid rising competition — **Vaibhav Taneja**
    *   Long-term normalized energy margins are expected in the mid-to-low 20% range — **Vaibhav Taneja**
*   **Service & Corporate Financials:**
    *   Service and other margins reached an all-time high of 14.1% (up from 9.2%), driven by used car volume, supercharging, service centers, insurance, and Robotaxi infrastructure investments — **Vaibhav Taneja**
