briefings.title: The Golden Age of Software Engineering | Scott Wu, Cognition | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: AI software engineering agents like Devin have advanced from 30-second chatbots to 16-hour autonomous workers capable of handling entire end-to-end tasks, enabling companies to 10x their shipped software output.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI software engineering agents like Devin have advanced from 30-second chatbots to 16-hour autonomous workers capable of handling entire end-to-end tasks, enabling companies to 10x their shipped software output.

## The Evolution of AI Coding Capabilities
* **Model Capability Explosion:** Evaluated using METR study benchmarks tracking unattended task length, AI models have progressed from 30-second tasks (GPT-3.5 / ChatGPT era) to tasks spanning 16 hours or multiple days.
* **Industry-Wide Progress:** Flagship models across all major AI labs have reached capability saturation, consistently executing complex, multi-step engineering tasks.
* **Closing the Loop:** Moving beyond tab-complete and code generation (GitHub Copilot era), agents now operate autonomously across the entire workflow:
  * **Understanding & Planning:** Analyzing codebases and planning changes.
  * **Testing & Review:** Utilizing computer/browser use to execute tests and perform code reviews independently.

## Organizational Transformation & Autonomous Operations
* **Cognition Case Study:** Cognition increased its engineering headcount by 40% (from ~45 to ~60) while **10x-ing** its shipped software volume over a 6-month period between November 2025 and April 2026.
* **Autonomous Session Kickoff:** At Cognition, over 90% of code is committed by Devin, and the majority of Devin sessions are now initiated asynchronously via automated triggers (e.g., performance monitoring, DataDog errors) rather than human prompts.
* **Event-Driven Workflows:** Teams are refactoring engineering organizations around parallel, event-driven execution:
  * **Bulk CVE Remediation:** Automated security vulnerability scanning and patching.
  * **Large-Scale Refactors:** Handling massive codebase upgrades file-by-file.
  * **Bug Triage:** Direct routing of customer reports to agents for automated pull request generation.

## Shifting Metrics: From Tokens to Business Outcomes
* **The "Token Maxing" Era:** Short-lived phase (January to May 2026) where organizations measured AI usage by token volume—noted by Uber burning through its entire annual token budget in just 3 months.
* **Outcome-Based Evaluation:** Measurement is shifting away from lines of code or token consumption toward actual business impact and project outcomes.
* **The Software Abundance Reality:** Rather than replacing human engineers, 10x productivity addresses the massive global backlog of unbuilt software across industries like finance (Goldman Sachs), automotive (Mercedes-Benz), retail (Lowe's), and healthcare (Elevance).

## Notable Quotes
> "What would you do with an infinite army of software engineers?"
> — **Scott Wu**

> "We're getting to a point where there's real saturation on a lot of tasks... all the models are good enough to just go and do these tasks."
> — **Scott Wu**

> "Every human software engineer is 10 times more productive, but guess what, we have 10 times more things to go build."
> — **Scott Wu**

briefings.title: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer testifies on Trump's trade policy agenda — 7/22/2026
briefings.tldr: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer testified before the Senate Finance Committee on the Trump administration's 2026 trade policy agenda, defending the use of targeted tariffs and reciprocal trade agreements to drive domestic re-industrialization, while bipartisan senators pushed back on rising consumer costs, trade disruptions, and agricultural strain.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer testified before the Senate Finance Committee on the Trump administration's 2026 trade policy agenda, defending the use of targeted tariffs and reciprocal trade agreements to drive domestic re-industrialization, while bipartisan senators pushed back on rising consumer costs, trade disruptions, and agricultural strain.

## Economic Indicators & Trade Deficits
- **Trade Deficit Reduction:** Ambassador Greer reported that the U.S. trade deficit in goods for the 12 months ending May 2026 decreased by 24% compared to the same period a year earlier, following the April 2025 implementation of the reciprocal trade program.
- **China Dependency:** The U.S. goods trade deficit with China fell to $200 billion in 2025 (the lowest since 2005), and China's share of total U.S. imports dropped to approximately 9% (the lowest since joining the WTO in 2001).
- **Manufacturing Metrics:** Manufacturing real wages increased by over $2,000 under President Trump, productivity surged 2.4% in Q4 2025, and manufacturing wages rose 4.7%. Capital goods accounted for 33% of imports in 2025 and 40% in 2026.
- **Inflation & Consumer Prices:** Greer cited a 0.4% drop in the Consumer Price Index in June (the largest decline since April 2020) and year-over-year core inflation at 2.6%. Conversely, Ranking Member Wyden cited estimates from the Congressional Budget Office and Treasury showing that 2025 tariffs cost the average American family $1,700.

## Reciprocal Trade Deals & Market Access
- **Global Agreements:** The U.S. currently has 19 framework or reciprocal trade deals covering 32% of global gross domestic product. Countries like Cambodia, Argentina, Malaysia, and Indonesia are implementing or scheduled to implement tariff reductions to zero.
- **USMCA Negotiations:** Ambassador Greer stated he is traveling to Mexico City to meet with President Claudia Sheinbaum and Secretary Marcelo Ebrard regarding ongoing USMCA negotiations, aiming for interim arrangements with Canada and Mexico by the end of the year.
- **Agricultural Trade:** Greer noted that the monthly agricultural trade deficit under President Biden ($6.2 billion) has fallen to under $3 billion under President Trump. However, Senators Bennet, Grassley, and others raised severe alarms over losses for soybean, corn, and wheat farmers facing high input costs and retaliatory risks.

## Tariffs, Authorities, and Legislation
- **Congressional Trade Powers Reform Act:** Ranking Member Wyden announced the introduction of the *Congressional Trade Powers Reform Act*, which would overhaul trade authorities and require congressional approval for any presidential tariff.
- **Canadian and Chinese Tariffs:** Debate centered on recent 50% tariffs announced on Canadian goods using a provision based on the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of 1930. Senators challenged whether Canadian goods would face higher tariffs than Chinese goods in certain sectors.
- **Tariff Refunds and Small Businesses:** Senators White House and Welch raised concerns that small businesses struggle to navigate Customs and Border Protection (CBP) online portals for tariff refunds, and that large corporations may retain refunds rather than passing them to consumers. Greer maintained that the CBP portal is user-friendly and that foreign/domestic importers of record can file for refunds.

## Sector-Specific Concerns & Supply Chains
- **Critical Minerals:** Discussions covered U.S. access to processed critical minerals and rare earths from China, as well as diversification efforts in Central Asia (Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan) and Indonesia (nickel and raw ore exports).
- **Agriculture and Inputs:** Senators raised specific regional issues including fertilizer and anhydrous ammonia supply (Grassley), Mexican pork investigations, Colorado farm losses (Bennet), Montana palladium mining under pressure from Russian dumping (Danes), Minnesota taconite and sugar quotas (Smith), Wyoming soda ash in India and beef/sheep markets (Barrasso), and Tennessee whiskey and timber (Blackburn).
- **Tourism and Aerospace:** Senators Cortez Masto and Welch highlighted a $14 billion trade deficit in travel/tourism in 2025 and raised concerns regarding Section 232 investigations impacting aerospace and aviation.

## Notable Quotes
> "The trade policy the president seeks to solve are generational. These things were not broken in a day, and they won't be fixed overnight, but they must be fixed. This is why I'm pleased to report that the combination of tariffs and deals core to the president's trade policy has yielded quick and impressive results."
> — **Ambassador Jamieson Greer**

> "Like so many other promises Donald Trump has made to working people, the second he set foot in the White House, he did nothing to put American businesses and workers first. What he did is he embarked on a tariff spree that put the cost of living crisis on steroids in America."
> — **Senator Ron Wyden**

> "The surplus and the deficit is a result of the fact that you have made it more expensive for us to buy products from other places. And it has absolutely nothing to do with the question I'm asking you..."
> — **Senator Michael Bennet**

briefings.title: Venki Ramakrishnan: The Science and Hype of Living Longer | Podcast | In Good Company

people.name: Venki Ramakrishnan
people.role: Nobel laureate in chemistry and author

briefings.tldr: Longevity hype overstates our ability to extend maximum human lifespan past the 120-year ceiling, but health span can be improved through moderate living, sleep, and exercise.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Longevity hype overstates our ability to extend maximum human lifespan past the 120-year ceiling, but health span can be improved through moderate living, sleep, and exercise. While tech billionaires invest billions into anti-aging ventures and cellular reprogramming, aging is an analog process driven by molecular and DNA damage that remains fundamentally difficult to hack.

## Defining Aging and the Human Lifespan Ceiling
* **Aging Definition:** **Gradual loss of function:** Sir Venki Ramakrishnan defines aging as the gradual loss of function across molecules, cells, tissues, and the entire body due to accumulated damage and changes over time.
* **The 120-Year Ceiling:** Average life expectancy has doubled over the last 150 years (rising from roughly 50 to 80), driven by public health, vaccinations, nutrition, and medicine tackling early-life infant mortality and infectious diseases.
* **Maximum Lifespan Limit:** The maximum human lifespan ceiling has barely moved; only one person has ever exceeded 120 years, and there is no physical or chemical law guaranteeing we can extend lifespans by hundreds of years.

## Cellular Damage, Repair, and the Hallmarks of Aging
* **DNA Damage as a Driver:** **Molecular deterioration:** Damage to DNA and mitochondria—caused by environmental exposure and normal cellular living—is fundamental and drives downstream dysfunction.
* **Cellular Senescence:** **Cancer defense mechanism:** Damaged cells enter senescence, failing to function normally and secreting inflammatory compounds. While this is an early-life cancer prevention mechanism to eliminate mutating cells, accumulated damage overwhelms the body's repair mechanisms with age.
* **Organ Aging:** Different organs age at different rates depending on individual genetics and lifestyle factors like smoking or drinking.

## The Science and Hype of Cellular Reprogramming
* **Cellular Reprogramming:** **Reversing biological age:** Inspired by John Gurdon cloning frogs via nuclear transfer and Shinya Yamanaka introducing four genes to revert cells into pluripotent stem cells, researchers are trying to wind back the developmental clock.
* **The Human Barrier:** **Safety and control challenges:** Implementing reprogramming safely in humans is extremely difficult because viral vectors or transgenic approaches produce heterogeneous results (some cells reprogram while others do not), and some involved genes are oncogenes capable of causing cancer.
* **Animal Model Reality:** While reprogrammed mice look healthier by various criteria, the interventions have not actually increased their overall lifespan.

## Billionaires, Longevity Startups, and Tech Bias
* **The Tech Industry Bias:** **Digital vs. Analog:** Tech billionaires who made fortunes in their 20s approach mortality as a software problem to be hacked, failing to recognize that biology operates in the messy analog world.
* **Altos Labs and Funding:** Backed by tech figures like Yuri Milner and Jeff Bezos with a $5 billion budget and top Nobel laureates, Altos Labs officially aims to extend health span ("die young after a long time"), though investors also bet on monetizing breakthrough longevity treatments.
* **Skepticism of Single-Subject Trials:** High-profile biohackers like Brian Johnson (spending $2 million/year) lack control experiments, mixing treatments that make it impossible to scientifically isolate what is working.
* **Skepticism of Fads:** Cryopreservation (freezing a thin mouse brain slice is the closest milestone achieved; freezing a live mouse and thawing it remains science fiction) and young blood transfusions are dismissed as high-markup hype without rigorous validation.

## Simple Habits for Health Span
* **Caloric Restriction:** **Metabolic recycling:** While strict caloric restriction causes constant hunger, eating moderately and controlling weight turns on pathways that recycle defective molecules and organelles. GLP1 drugs show potential for metabolic health, though side effects like muscle loss require safe administration.
* **Sleep:** **Repair cycles:** Getting adequate sleep (Ramakrishnan aims for 8 hours) is vital because much of the body's cellular recycling and repair happens during the sleep cycle.
* **Exercise:** **Tissue regeneration:** Combining weight training and cardio (such as cross-trainer elliptical work mimicking cross-country skiing) stimulates tissue regeneration and counters functional decline.

## Societal Ethics and the Two-Tiered Future
* **Generational Turnover:** **Societal stagnation:** Doubling lifespans combined with dropping fertility rates would halt generational turnover, leaving entrenched older populations in control of wealth, power, and political systems.
* **The Multi-Tiered Society:** **Disparity in years and power:** Advanced longevity treatments risk creating a two-tier society where wealthy individuals buy extended lives and deeper power advantages, widening the 10-to-15-year life expectancy gap already seen between rich and poor populations (e.g., in the US and UK).

## Notable Quotes
* > "Plan A is simply to try not to die. Plan B is to try to believe that even if you die, your whole body will be resurrected and you will go to some paradise. And plan C is that maybe your body will decay but you will have an immortal soul..." — Sir Venki Ramakrishnan
* > "The people who are funding it are interested in two things. One is they think there's a lot of money in aging... but the other strategy is deep down they think, well, maybe these guys will crack the problem and, you know, maybe we'll end up living not forever, but maybe a much longer time." — Sir Venki Ramakrishnan
* > "I think they have that bias whether it's conscious or not. They do have the bias of looking at the entire world as if it's a software problem... and the world is not digital the world is analog and I think they simply don't want to want to confront that." — Sir Venki Ramakrishnan
* > "Everything is not about living longer. It's about enjoying life while you have it." — Sir Venki Ramakrishnan

briefings.title: Vibe Coding for the Next Billion | Michele Catasta, Replit | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: Replit President and Head of AI Michele Catasta and founding partner Max Corbani discuss how AI development environments and vibe coding are transforming 60 million non-technical users into software and agent builders.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Replit President and Head of AI Michele Catasta and founding partner Max Corbani discuss how AI development environments and vibe coding are transforming 60 million non-technical users into software and agent builders.

## Journey to Vibe Coding and Democratizing Software
* **Background and Mission:** Michele Catasta started hacking open source at age 16 in Italy and spent 15 years pursuing the idea of making machines write code, eventually doing a PhD in deep learning at EPFL in Lausanne and applying Transformers to source code at Stanford.
* **Early Shipping Strategy:** Catasta recommends that builders ship AI products as soon as they have basic reliability, noting that Replit generated thousands of versions of a simple cat image web app before achieving end-to-end reliability.
* **Replit Agent Launch:** Replit shipped its AI agent in September 2024—six months before Andre Karpathy coined the term "vibe coding."
* **Current Scale:** Replit has crossed half a billion in ARR, serves over 60 million users, and is targeting $1 billion in revenue by the end of the year.

## User Base and the Rise of the Agent Manager
* **Citizen Developers:** Replit's adoption spans 1.5 billion Excel-trained knowledge workers across departments like HR, go-to-market, and support who need to build software solutions to automate work.
* **General-Purpose Product Strategy:** Rejecting the temptation to target a single narrow persona during product-market fit, Replit maintained a general-purpose agent philosophy to serve diverse departments.
* **The Agent Manager Paradigm:** Catasta notes that since 2025, every human is becoming an "agent manager" whose daily job involves prioritizing tasks, running multiple agents in parallel, validating results, and delegating work instead of executing steps manually.

## AI Models and Open Source Strategy
* **Shift to Heterogeneous Models:** Replit initially relied entirely on closed-source frontier models to avoid capital-intensive training, but the strategy has flipped as open-weights models become impressively capable for vibe coding.
* **Task-Specific Intelligence:** Catasta emphasizes that intelligence is not one-size-fits-all; Replit maps specific models to specific user tasks using a mix of self-fine-tuned models, open-weights models, and closed frontier models.
* **Industry Benchmarks:** Replit recently launched *Vibe Bench*, a new benchmark specifically designed to measure vibe coding capabilities.

## The Future: From Apps to Autonomous Agents
* **Disappearance of Traditional Apps:** Catasta predicts that traditional software applications and UIs will slowly disappear as humans shift from manual data input to discussing, planning, and delegating end-to-end tasks to agents.
* **High-Level Goal Execution:** Replit's next evolution will allow users to specify high-level business goals—such as achieving a 5% conversion rate on a SaaS app—and let autonomous agents handle the execution, testing, and modifications.
* **Workplace Impact:** While some job displacement will occur during the transition phase, agents will upgrade daily human work by removing tedious tasks like triaging emails and Slack, enabling leaner companies and new business creation.

## Notable Quotes
> "If there is someone out there who cares, do it because you're going to start to get feedback, as long as it's not completely janky." — Michele Catasta
> 
> "Every single day you wake up and you have a long list of tasks in mind that you want to accomplish... And now you just dispatch agents to make that happen. So, your job is more trying to figure out, 'Okay, I'm going to prioritize these 10 different tasks. I'm going to run several agents in parallel.'" — Michele Catasta
> 
> "Apps are going to start to slowly disappear. And what I mean by that, we built applications, we built UIs for the last decades because that is the only way that we've been used to interact with computers... The future that I foresee happening, maybe much faster than a lot of people expect, is, we're going to start to build way more agents than actually applications." — Michele Catasta

briefings.title: Why Ambitious Startup Ideas Are Actually Easier To Sell
briefings.tldr: James Hawkins explains how PostHog transformed from an open-source product analytics tool into an AI-native, self-driving software platform by increasing founder ambition, automating product management loops, and embracing high-upside market strategies.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
James Hawkins explains how PostHog transformed from an open-source product analytics tool into an AI-native, self-driving software platform by increasing founder ambition, automating product management loops, and embracing high-upside market strategies.

## PostHog’s AI-Native Transformation
- **Shift to Self-Driving Software:** PostHog evolved from providing academic analytics to actually solving jobs for users and improving graphs automatically.
- **The Recursive AI Loop:** James Hawkins describes how the system ingests data types like support tickets, video clips, and Slack discussions to ship pull requests automatically.
- **Traction and Metrics:** 
  - PostHog's newly shipped support product has roughly **1,100 companies** using it.
  - A significant chunk of PostHog's own engineering pull requests are now generated via this AI loop.

## The Product Engineering Challenge & The Intent Harness
- **The Thousand Tiny Features Problem:** The risk of AI building numerous disjointed features is mitigated by focusing on the "intent side" of product engineering.
- **The Limitations of Current Harnesses:** Existing tools like Claude lack conversational product context; PostHog is working on broad harnesses that capture the actual product vision from engineers and leadership.
- **Redefining Roles:** 
  - Product managers transition into configuring software and setting rules and policies.
  - Support team roles evolve into writing manuals, rule books, and guiding the AI agents.

## Founder Dynamics & Co-CEO Roles
- **Job Swapping:** James Hawkins and co-founder Tim swapped roles (switching between CEO/CTO and product/sales responsibilities) to regain energy and leverage their evolving strengths.
- **Division of Labor for AI Pivot:** To execute the AI pivot smoothly without creating misaligned bottlenecks, Tim handled operations, finance, scaling, and hiring (more than doubling the company size that year), while James went "all in" on AI engineering.
- **Avoiding Burnout:** Building a big company requires long-term growth, which James and Tim believe is unsustainable if the work is not fundamentally fun.

## European vs. American Ambition & Fundraising
- **Breaking Imposter Syndrome:** Early on, the founders suffered from intense imposter syndrome, but Y Combinator normalized the reality that even massive companies are run by ordinary human beings.
- **Cultural Differences in Risk:** 
  - European founders often focus heavily on downside risks (e.g., failure, social perception, early GDPR compliance).
  - American culture encourages aiming for massive upside—such as declaring an intent to cure all disease.
- **Venture Capital Realities:** Startups are "default screwed anyway," meaning investors care exclusively about the **99.99% upside** (e.g., Y Combinator investing in 7,000 companies where 90% of total returns come from just 5 companies).

## Building a Cult Brand & The Pivot Journey
- **Intentional Differentiation:** In crowded markets, the challenge is standing out rather than creating demand; PostHog used distinct branding (like hedgehogs and bus ads), transparent pricing, and direct credit-card sign-ups to attract engineers.
- **The Pivot History:** PostHog executed **5 pivots** before landing on product analytics during the YC Winter 20 batch.
- **Validation Discipline:** The founders committed blindly and worked hard on each idea—visiting early customers in person via multiple trains and buses—before moving on when they repeatedly hit insurmountable product validation hurdles.

## Notable Quotes
> "You're default screwed as a startup. So, it is all upside. You just can't win on downside. The investors we want to work with are focused on the 'what if it all works out' because they know that 99.99% of your startup's upside hasn't been done yet." — James Hawkins

> "The role of our support team is becoming—and I really mean this, not just to sound nice—you're supporting the agents to do their job. So you're writing out the manual, the rule book, and you're iterating and improving, and you're kind of becoming a philosopher for support basically." — James Hawkins

> "Don't be a lemming. I think people have a really high propensity to do what society expects of you, which is to follow a career path that takes you... you go get a good degree at university, you become a banker, you gradually make a VP and then you retire and die. You really don't have to." — James Hawkins
